haiku-low.q1: The scheduler starts the controller at 02:00 UTC. The run reads replica rows with updated_at after hwm minus 2 hours, or the backfill start, up to the 02:00 cutoff.
haiku-low.q2: NOT STATED for bulk imports. The document says rows can become visible on the replica after their updated_at, by up to 90 minutes.
haiku-low.q3: The edit sets a later updated_at. The next nightly extract reads it, and the MERGE updates the stored row because the staged winner is newer.
haiku-low.q4: deleted_at is set, so the winning staged row gets is_deleted true and is merged. The row is never hard-deleted and stays in orders as flagged.
haiku-low.q5: The attempt writes a failed row with the error. The controller waits 15 minutes and retries with the same run_id and cutoff, up to three attempts, then pages on-call.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the last committed good night, never a partial one. A staleness alert is posted to the data-alerts channel. The owner who acts on it is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation finds the day differs with the stored version older, so it reloads that creation day from the replica under a reload run_id.
haiku-low.q8: The MERGE updates an existing order only when the staged winner has a later updated_at, or equal updated_at and larger row hash. Otherwise the stored row is left alone.
haiku-low.q9: It is stored in etl_watermark, one row. The value is the cutoff of the last committed nightly run, written in the same transaction as the MERGE, only if later.
haiku-low.q10: One warehouse transaction commits the MERGE, the hwm move and the success row together, or rolls back all three. Dashboards read only orders.
haiku-low.q11: The retry deletes that run_id's staged rows before loading again. It uses the same run_id and cutoff, so the window is hwm minus 2 hours up to the cutoff.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads the full extract of that creation day from the replica, ignoring the updated_at window, and applies steps 4 to 6 with the MERGE rule. It does not move the hwm.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler starts the controller at 02:00 UTC, which creates a run_id and starts attempt 1 with cutoff 02:00 UTC. It extracts from the read replica every row with updated_at after (hwm minus 2 hours) and at or before the cutoff. On the first run, with no hwm, the start is the configured backfill start.
sonnet.q2: NOT STATED for bulk imports specifically. The document says some rows become visible on the replica after their updated_at, up to 90 minutes late, and the 2-hour lookback covers that with a margin. It gives no reason why.
sonnet.q3: The edit sets a new updated_at. The next nightly extract (window starts at hwm minus 2h) picks it up. It is staged, wins as the newest version, and the MERGE updates the existing orders row because it beats the stored row.
sonnet.q4: A delete is a write that sets updated_at and deleted_at. The deleted version is the newest, so it wins. The row stays in orders and is flagged is_deleted = true. Rows are never removed.
sonnet.q5: The attempt writes a failed row with the error to etl_run_log in its own statement. If the process died without writing one, the controller writes it. If fewer than 3 attempts have started, the controller waits 15 minutes and starts the next attempt with the same run_id and cutoff. After the third failure it pages on-call with the run_id and last error. orders and the hwm are unchanged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the last good (previously committed) night. The 06:00 UTC check finds no nightly success row for the 02:00 cutoff and posts a staleness alert to the data-alerts channel. Who acts on it is not stated. If retries were exhausted, on-call was also paged.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares count and checksum of order_id plus updated_at per creation day over the last 30 days, replica vs orders. If the order is missing or older in orders, it reloads that day with a full extract of that creation day, under a new run_id with run kind reload.
sonnet.q8: Within a run, one winner is kept per order_id: later updated_at wins, and a tie goes to the larger row hash. The MERGE inserts new ids and updates an existing id only if the staged winner beats the stored row (later updated_at, ties to larger row hash). Otherwise the stored row is left alone.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse table etl_watermark, which has one row. The value is the run's cutoff (02:00 UTC). It is written only for a nightly run, inside the commit transaction together with the MERGE and the success row, and only if the cutoff is later than the stored value.
sonnet.q10: The MERGE into orders, the hwm update and the success row happen in one warehouse transaction that commits in full or rolls back. Dashboards read only orders, so they see the last committed night and never a partial one.
sonnet.q11: The retry deletes the rows for its run_id in orders_stage before bulk loading, so nothing is doubled, and other runs' rows are untouched. The retry has the same run_id and cutoff. The window is hwm minus 2 hours up to the cutoff. The hwm is unchanged because the failed attempt did not commit.
sonnet.q12: It does a full extract of that creation day from the replica, ignoring the updated_at window. It runs steps 4 to 6 (stage, pick winners, commit) under a new run_id with run kind reload. The same MERGE rule applies, so the newer replica version replaces the stale stored row. It does not change the hwm.
